media.title: Heritage Minutes: Wilder Penfield

timecodes.what: At kf_003.jpg (12.8s) (widescreen camera frame), Historica Canada's recording states "[plates crashing on floor] Every time she has a seizure, she smells something burning." — providing spoken context for 1937 Montreal Teaching Suite: Wilder Penfield's Numbered Cortical Ticket Model Beside the Giant-Handed Homunculus Sculpture.

Mid-segment 4:3 camera frame at kf_005.jpg (25.8s) as narration explains "Now, if we can provoke that smell by probing the surface of the brain, we’ll find the source of the seizures. Mrs. Gold, do you feel anything?", clarifying key empirical findings in Wilder Penfield & Edwin Boldrey's 1937 Brain Awake Cortical Stimulation Mapping of 126 Epilepsy Patients (Updated by Gordon et al., 2023 Nature).

Around kf_010.jpg (34.3s) (dark-backdrop stage / studio camera frame), commentary states "I can see the most wonderful lights. And now what do you feel? Did you pour cold water on my hand, Dr. Penfield?", connecting the empirical results to broader cognitive and neural science.
